arch_acc_nbcRevolving: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B 3.4.6.15 (identical wording in BCBC 2024, NBC(AE) 2023 and VBBL 2025 Book I, compared word by word from repo copies): (1) a revolving door, if used, shall 'a) be collapsible, b) have hinged doors providing equivalent exiting capacity located adjacent to it, c) be used as an exit from the ground floor level only, d) not be used at the foot of any stairway', e) glass to CAN/CGSB-12.1 'Safety Glazing' or CAN/CGSB-12.11-M 'Wired Safety Glass'; (2) 'a revolving door shall not be considered to have an exiting capacity for more than 45 persons'; (3) electrically powered revolving doors exempt if leaves collapse under the 3.4.6.16.(2) force, open from inside 'without requiring keys, special devices, or specialized knowledge', capacity from collapsed clear width, signs 1000–1500 mm — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt (PDF pp. 3-153 to 3-154)
arch_acc_nbcDoorRelease: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B (identical BCBC 2024, NBC(AE) 2023; VBBL adds, see arch_acc_vbblMaglock): 3.3.1.13.(2) 'a door in an access to exit shall be readily openable in travelling to an exit without requiring keys, special devices or specialized knowledge of the door-opening mechanism'; (7) such a door 'is permitted to be equipped with an electromagnetic lock conforming to Sentence 3.4.6.16.(5) or (6)'; 3.4.6.16.(1) principal entrance and exit doors openable from inside 'with not more than one releasing operation'; (5) electromagnetic locks without latches permitted, except on doors 'leading directly from a high-hazard industrial occupancy', provided a) fire alarm system, b) 'the locking device releases upon actuation of the alarm signal from the building's fire alarm system', c) 'releases immediately upon loss of power', d) manual switch 'readily accessible only to authorized personnel', e) 'a force of not more than 90 N applied to the door opening hardware initiates an irreversible process that will release the locking device within 15 s', g)-h) visual and tactile signs, i) 'the total time delay for all electromagnetic locks in any path of egress to release is not more than 15 s', k) emergency lighting; (6) B-2/B-3 version incl. switch 'at a constantly attended location within the locked space'; (7) hardware 900–1100 mm; 3.4.6.17 key-locked exits for banks and retail only; Note A-3.4.6.16.(5) maglocks 'are intended for use where there is a need for security additional to that provided by traditional exit hardware. They are not intended for indiscriminate use'; 'one switch will release and reset all devices simultaneously' — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt (PDF pp. 3-121, 3-154 to 3-156, 3-264)
arch_acc_vbblMaglock: RULE (Vancouver only): VBBL 2025 Book I Div. B: 3.4.6.16.(8) 'As an alternative to the requirements of Clauses (e), (f) and (g) in Sentence (5), acceptable door release hardware for an electromagnetic lock shall be located in close proximity to the egress door' with a push button plus motion sensor or pressure pad releasing immediately, a push button 'directly connected to the electrical circuit that provides power to the locking device', embossed 'EXIT' ≥25 mm, LED lit, labelled 'DOOR RELEASE', and a lock that resets automatically not before 15 s and only manually after fire alarm; 3.4.6.16.(1) also excepts 3.4.6.20 (security gates in front of exterior exit doors per the Fire By-law, A, D, E, F-2, F-3 only); 3.3.1.13.(11) maglocks on egress doors through Group D suites where acceptable to the CBO; Note A-3.3.1.13.(7) designers 'are to demonstrate that the requirements of the By-law have been met. This demonstration is to include a sequence of operation for the installation of any new maglocks and similar security devices that could singly or in combination, prevent, impede, or otherwise delay occupant egress or emergency responder access' — data/raw/codes/vbbl2025_v1.txt
arch_acc_nbcObstruction: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B (same BCBC 2024, NBC(AE) 2023): 3.3.1.24.(1) 'No obstruction shall be permitted in any occupancy that would restrict the width of a normal means of egress from any part of a floor area to less than 750 mm unless an alternative means of egress is provided adjacent to, accessible from, and plainly visible from the obstructed means of egress'; Note A-3.3.1.24.(1) 'Obstructions including posts, counters or turnstiles should not be located in a manner that would restrict the width of a normal means of egress'; 3.4.3.3.(1) 'no fixture, turnstile or construction shall project into or be fixed within the required width of an exit' — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt (pp. 3-125, 3-151)
arch_acc_nbcAccessible: RULE: NBC 2020 Div. B Section 3.8 (NBC(AE) 2023 same; BCBC 2024 says 'accessible' for 'barrier-free'; VBBL 3.8.2.7 same as BCBC): 3.8.2.2.(1) 'all pedestrian entrances … shall be barrier-free [accessible]' except service entrances; (3) only one doorway per entrance need comply; 3.8.2.3.(1) path of travel 'within all other normally occupied floor areas'; (2) not required to service rooms, service spaces, etc.; BCBC (2)(i) not within high-hazard industrial occupancies; 3.8.2.7.(1) power door operators on self-closing doors at entrances incl. vestibule inner doors and on the path to rooms off a public corridor; 3.8.3.6.(2) doorways 'clear width not less than 850 mm' (BCBC: measured at 90° to the stop); (6) operator controls 900–1100 mm and 150–300 mm — data/raw/codes/nbc.txt, bcbc2024.txt

arch_acc_opcBiometrics: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, 'Guidance for processing biometrics – for businesses', 2025-08-11 (PIPEDA): 'Biometric information that can uniquely identify an individual is sensitive information'; 'express consent would be the appropriate form of consent'; for non-essential uses 'you must provide individuals with other means of access or participation'; assess 'less intrusive means'; example 'the use of a fingerprint to gain access to a building'; 'Use verification over identification, where possible'; 'avoid creating large, centralized databases of biometric information if alternatives are viable' — https://www.priv.gc.ca/en/privacy-topics/health-genetic-and-other-body-information/biometrics/gd_bio_org-final
